## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by pale tan to brownish wings with delicate darker lines and a slender triangular resting posture typical of many aquatic or wetland-associated Samea moths. In Florida, Samea druchachalis is recorded from wetland habitats and is likely found around ponds, marshes, canals, ditches, and vegetated freshwater edges where adults may come to lights. Its larval host plants appear poorly documented compared with the better-known waterlettuce moth Samea multiplicalis, so it is best treated cautiously as a small wetland-associated moth whose caterpillars likely feed on aquatic or semi-aquatic vegetation and whose adults and larvae support spiders, bats, birds, fishes, and parasitoid wasps.
